A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoLA research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and matchable, including appendices A–H in v2 and A–I in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original LoLA recall and commonsense evaluations, scoring ablations, efficiency measurements, and kernel-spectrum simulations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds LongBench evaluations, cache-access ablations, and further latency and throughput measurements.

M1.justification: The three memory systems, SRE-based selection, state updates, and attention computation are retained. Chunkwise inference already appears in v2 Section 3; v3's additional explanations and chunkwise pseudocode document that existing procedure.

E1.justification: V3 Appendix C adds LongBench evaluation on QasperQA, MultiFieldQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, Musique, TREC, and TriviaQA. These introduce substantial long-document QA and few-shot coverage beyond the retained RULER and commonsense evaluations.

E2.justification: V3 adds Llama-3.1-8B to the extended RULER comparison in Table 2 and pure linear attention to the efficiency comparison in Appendix B. The commonsense baselines and scoring-ablation alternatives remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V3 introduces restricted-query controls with 50-sample ablations, layer timing at sequence and embedding dimensions 4096 with 32 heads and batch size two, and decoding measurements after 1K-context prefill. It also adds LongBench cache configurations, a 1024-token LoLCATs window in Table 1, and a 50-sample-per-task Llama reference in Table 2. Existing training settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix I tests whether benefits depend on the hidden state, sparse cache, or their combination by restricting query access while retaining cache updates. Appendix B extends the existing efficiency analysis with layer-latency and decoding-throughput sensitivity studies. Earlier scoring and collision analyses remain.

E5.justification: V3 Table 7 specifies averaging over 250 trials for the new layer-latency experiment. The existing TTFT experiment retains its 100-trial specification; this does not establish increased repetition of earlier experiments. Accuracy uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: V3 adds LongBench results, including averages of 27.8 for LoLA, 9.0 for extended LoLCATs, and 36.1 for Mamba2, alongside new baseline, cache-ablation, and timing results. Table 1 changes LoLA's S-NIAH-1 accuracy at 4K with cache sizes (512,512) from 99.9% to 100%, while corresponding appendix entries retain 99.0%; this discrepancy is unexplained.

T1.justification: V3 Appendix D adds mathematical formulations for online regression, nested cache selection, and time-weighted gating in Equations 16–18. Appendix E's SVD argument is retained. The new Equations 16–17 contain indexing ambiguities, summing over i while using k_t and v_t.

C1.justification: The headline contributions remain training-free SRE-guided sparse caching, mitigation of memory collisions, retrieval improvement from 0.6% to 97.4% with a 4.6-times smaller cache, and stronger 1B/8B commonsense performance. Added experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands explanations connecting SRE to test-time training and distinguishing sparse preservation from gating. It interprets the new cache-access ablations, discusses LongBench distillation shortfalls and prefill-versus-decoding costs, and explicitly limits experimental validation to two LoLCATs base models.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds chunkwise pseudocode and replaces v2's promise of future full code with a link to a minimal PyTorch implementation. Appendix B clarifies the PyTorch implementation used for timing comparisons. V2's standalone reproducibility statement and explicit released-weight access note are removed.

R1.justification: Appendix D substantially expands positioning through test-time training and an intra-head/inter-head/inter-layer hybrid taxonomy. It adds comparisons with B'MOJO, SE-Attn, HAX, Gated Linear Attention, and Lattice, among others. The DeltaProduct discussion and citation are removed.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording and organizational revisions: clearer chunking explanations, separate Section 4.4 for scoring ablations, additional appendix subheadings, and revised limitations and reproducibility organization. The abstract and overall main-text narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The document is globally reformatted for TMLR, changing typography, margins, headers, and author layout. Four tables are added, Tables 1–2 gain rows or grouping, and existing displays are redistributed; Figures 8–9 now share a page. The ten figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses important validation gaps through LongBench evaluations and controlled cache-access ablations, strengthening assessment of practical applicability and the proposed mechanism beyond v2's evidence. Added reference comparisons, efficiency measurements, and chunkwise reproduction guidance further improve assessability. These gains outweigh the remaining underspecified LongBench protocol, inconsistent retrieval entries, and indexing problems in the new formal objectives.
